loops.text: access token expires while the tab is backgrounded

construction_notes: Control: mostly one technical thread. One brief calendar interruption. Not optimized for any resolver. Includes a second AUTH loop so later probes can be loop-ambiguous without cross-domain noise.

turns.text: hey — the refresh call is still giving me 401. same payload we used last week.
Ok. Is this the `/auth/refresh` path with the rotating refresh cookie, or the old body-token one?
rotating cookie. access token looks fine for ~12 min then boom, 401, refresh returns 401 too.
That's a different smell than a dead access token. If refresh itself 401s, cookie reuse or family-id mismatch is more likely than expiry.
i did see the access token go stale if I leave the tab in the background. that's maybe a second thing.
Splitting them: (1) refresh 401, (2) backgrounded tab / expired access token. Don't mix the logs.
yeah. for the 401 after refresh — Set-Cookie on the refresh response looks empty in chrome.
Empty Set-Cookie often means SameSite / Secure / wrong domain. Check whether the API is on `api.` and the app on apex.
api.internal.example, app is app.internal.example. we set Domain=.internal.example
Then look at whether refresh is going through a gateway that strips Set-Cookie. I've seen nginx proxy_cookie_path eat these.
ugh maybe. the 401 body says `refresh_reuse_detected` sometimes, not always.
Reuse detection firing intermittently is consistent with two tabs racing refresh.
I did have staging open in another window. damn.
Close one, retry with a single tab, and paste the refresh request/response headers (redact the cookie value).
single tab now. still 401. wait, different code: `invalid_refresh`.
So not reuse this time. Cookie not arriving, or server rotated already. Network tab: is the cookie attached on the refresh request?
it's attached. httponly. length looks right.
Then server-side store vs JWT refresh. If you persist jti in redis, check TTL vs cookie max-age.
redis ttl is 7d, cookie is 7d. i'm going to dump the jti from the cookie vs redis.
Good. Keep the background-tab expiry as a separate note so we don't 'fix' it by accident.
jti is in redis. so why 401
Clock skew, or you're hashing a different secret on the refresh service than issue. Compare kid.
did standup move to 10:15 or are we still 9:45
I don't have the calendar. Last you told me it was 9:45; I wouldn't treat that as source of truth.
whatever, I'll ping Priya. kid is the same on both services actually
Back on refresh 401: next is audience/issuer claim. Easy to mismatch after a gateway rewrite.
iss is https://auth.internal.example on both. this is annoying.
Try issuing a refresh from curl with the same cookie the browser has. Isolates chrome vs API.
curl works. so it's the browser. what the hell
Then look at fetch credentials and CSRF. A working curl + failing SPA is often `credentials: 'omit'` on one client path.
there's a fetch wrapper for 'silent refresh' that might not pass credentials
That would 401 refresh in the app and succeed in curl. Check that wrapper before more redis archaeology.
ok found it. credentials omit on the silent path. the 'normal' login path is include.
That's enough to explain the refresh 401. The backgrounded access-token expiry is still open.
we can leave the background one. remind me what we actually changed for the 401
You hadn't patched yet in this thread — you found silent refresh using credentials omit vs include on login. That's the candidate fix, not redis TTL.
right. and the other one we just parked
Parked: access token dying when the tab is backgrounded. Separate from the refresh 401.
